content.comment_body: Hello everyone, [article_no] [product_name] FW [version_no] Previously, I used the cursor key to view temperatures and other results. Now, I can’t access this function anymore. I suspect it’s a hardware issue. I upgraded the firmware, hoping it would resolve the problem, but it didn’t help. Any thoughts? I’ve attached my program routine. Thanks in advance.
If your program uses cursor keys, you need to press both the cursor key and ESC key together to activate the function.

The issue is related to message text activation. When you want a message text to appear by pressing cursor keys (along with ESC), a message text has to be active for this combination to work. If none is active, pressing ESC brings up the system menu. In your situation, you should program a message text with the lowest priority (0) that remains always active. The text can be something generic, such as "Start screen" or your company name, etc.
Hello [user_name], Your explanation is clear. I’ll implement this in my routine. Thanks.

Hello [user_name], Unfortunately, it didn’t resolve the issue. Still, I appreciate your help. I’ll report any additional problems I encounter. I’m experiencing something related to analog input ripple and will start a new discussion for that. This is my first [product_name] project, so I might be missing some key steps. Regards
I updated your program with my suggested changes and tested it on my [product_name]. It works exactly as described.
Yes, it’s working now! Thank you!

analysis.insight_summary: A user had trouble accessing display functions using the cursor key on their [product_name], even after updating firmware. The issue was resolved by activating an appropriate message text and using the ESC and cursor key combination. After applying the advised changes, the user confirmed the functionality now works properly.
